text.cf3199875810: How easy it is to compress a substance: how much its volume decreases with increasing pressure and a constant temperature. Gases are easily compressed (large κT), liquids and solids are almost not (very small κT).
text.fa0c08ec86cc: How much the air is "filled" with water vapor compared to the maximum it can hold at that temperature, as a percentage. 100% — the air is saturated (further fog or dew); 0% - the air is completely dry. Warm air holds more vapor than cold air.
text.5b3a88eebc0f: How much the real behavior of matter differs from the "ideal gas" from school physics (pV=nRT). Z=1 — the substance behaves exactly like an ideal gas. Z is significantly different from 1 - molecules "feel" each other (attract or repel), and the school formula cannot be applied.
text.38de495a4bb2: How much does a substance resist flow — how hard is it to make one layer of liquid or vapor slide past the next one. Honey is more viscous than water, water is more viscous than air. The higher the viscosity, the more energy is lost to friction in the pipe.
text.9cb212272c27: How strongly the pressure increases inside a substance heated in a completely sealed rigid vessel, where the volume cannot change. Therefore, a bottle filled to the brim and tightly closed with liquid may crack from heating.

text.3ee0adba7a67: How much energy the cycle produces or consumes per second (kilowatts = kilojoules per second) depends both on the work done for each kilogram of the working body and on how many kilograms pass through the installation every second (mass flow rate).

accuracy.title: Sensitivity to input rounding

accuracy.limits: This is a local linear estimate, not a guaranteed error interval. Instrument uncertainty and model accuracy are excluded; phase and region crossings are not checked. accuracy.mixture: Phase boundaries and mixtures need separate analysis; single-phase derivatives do not apply here.
accuracy.singular: The Jacobian is singular or derivatives are unavailable. Suggested digits cannot be determined.

p05.transport.heading: IAPWS-95 transport validity ranges
p05.transport.mu: Viscosity, R12-08: up to 300 MPa — 1173.15 K; 300…350 MPa — 873.15 K; 350…500 MPa — 433.15 K; 500…1000 MPa — 373.15 K. Each pressure cutoff belongs to the preceding interval.
p05.transport.lambda: Conductivity, R15-11: up to 100 MPa — 1173.15 K; 100…250 MPa — 874 K; 250…687 MPa — 573 K; 687…785 MPa — 403 K; 785…1000 MPa — 348 K. Each pressure cutoff belongs to the preceding interval.
p05.transport.lower: All intervals start at the melting curve. Vapor below the triple-point pressure requires T ≥ 273.16 K. Kinematic viscosity needs viscosity, thermal diffusivity needs conductivity, and Prandtl number needs both. A dash means unavailable, not zero.
p05.unavailable.prefix: Outside this IAPWS-95 property range: T ≤

p05.subtriple.vapor: IAPWS-95: vapor below 273.16 K requires extrapolation, which is not implemented here.
